ground_truth.unit: logit coefficient per real dollar of sugar-industry contributions
ground_truth.location: Table 1, District fixed effects, Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("The Determinants of Voting in Favor of Sugar Reform"), column District fixed effects, row Inflation-adjusted sugar contributions.  Logit; the dependent variable equals 1 for "aye" votes on the two reform amendments to the U.S. sugar program (the 2013 Pitts amendment, H. Amdt. 227 to H.R. 1947, and the 2018 Foxx amendment, H. Amdt. 605 to H.R. 2; aye = a vote against sugar interests) and 0 otherwise.  One observation per House district and vote; the two votes are treated as repeated votes on the same issue. Regressor: inflation-adjusted sugar-industry contributions (all sugar-industry PACs plus individual contributions over $200 from people working in the sugar industry, Center for Responsive Politics) to the incumbent, aggregated from one year before the vote through the end of the calendar year of the vote.  Controls: the American Conservative Union ideology score (ACU, 1-100, higher = more conservative), tenure, the district poverty rate, % with a bachelor's degree, median income, % population over 65, and a dummy for membership on the House agriculture committee.  District fixed effects, so only the districts whose vote outcome changed between the two amendments identify the coefficients.  Probability values from robust standard errors; the table prints coefficient (p), p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 1 (robust SEs reproduction), -0.0006, p < 0.001.

Robust standard errors; the table prints p = 0.001, significant at 1%.

i4r.notes: DP 57 Table 1 col 2, -0.0004, p < 0.001 (the meta-database row's r_coeff "-.004" is a slip).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Inflation adjustment: data contributions are nominal integers; 2018 contributions deflated to 2013 dollars with CPI-U annual averages (232.957/251.107). The paper does not state the deflator or base year.

Window mapping assumed from the paper's order of description: SugarReplicate.dta = baseline window (1 year before vote to end of vote's calendar year), SugarReplicate_iter1.dta = calendar year of vote, SugarReplicate_iter2.dta = 12 months before vote. The contribution variable used is totalcont (the only column that differs across files); sugcont (identical across files) is not used.

Outcome coded 1 for Aye, 0 otherwise (No, No Vote, Not Voting), following the table note; this yields 94 switching districts, 93 after listwise deletion on missing covariates (186 obs), and 53 switching incumbents (same cid in both Congresses; 106 obs).

FE logit estimated as unconditional logit with FE dummies (glm, binomial) on units whose outcome varies, mirroring Stata logit with i.FE; robust HC0 p-values printed for information. The agriculture-committee coefficient is not identified (quasi-separation), as in the paper's -36/-39.
deviations_stdout: inflation adjustment uses CPI-U annual averages, 2018 contributions in 2013 dollars (paper does not state deflator/base year)
mapping of data files to windows assumed: SugarReplicate.dta = baseline, _iter1 = calendar year, _iter2 = 12 months before vote
cell.notes: Three exploratory runs (variable inspection, window/file comparison, switching-unit counts; no RESULT lines), then one estimation run, which is the final run. No claim or error attempts. Controls: ACU (ncu), tenure, poverty, bach, medincome, over65, agcom. District FE = id (state*100+district); incumbent FE = cid restricted to members appearing in both Congresses. Results match Table 1 closely (pseudo R2 0.746/0.723 vs 0.745/0.721; poverty 2.19, bach 1.21, over65 -1.87 in the district-FE column).
